summary: T. W. Rhys Davids worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a Ph.D. from the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He held posts at the University of London (1882–1904) and the University of Manchester (1904–1915).

Tadao Yoshikawa specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University (~1955–1964). His academic career included faculty appointments at Kyoto University (1974, 1984–2000) and Ryukoku University (2002), and he presided over the Toho Gakkai (~2007–2011).

Tadashi Inoue was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1956). He served at Kyoto National Museum (1967, 1979), Iida City Museum (1988–2006), Nara University (1987), and Bukkyo University (1995).

Tadashi Sekino was a scholar in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1892 to 1895 and later served there as professor emeritus from ~1929 to 1935.

Tadashi Tani worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University, studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama (1995), and served as a professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under teachers Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completing his Ph.D. at the University of London in 1978. He held appointments at SOAS University of London, including Professor (attested 1987–1996) and Reader (attested 2005).
Tai-shing Wut specialized in Buddhist studies and earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998).

Taichiro Kobayashi worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Kyoto University (1919–1923) under Sentaro Sawamura, Kitaro Nishida, and others. He later held posts at the Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts and Kobe University (1950).

Taido Kitamura worked in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. His career included an appointment at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and further affiliation attested 1994–1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned degrees from Columbia University and the Graduate Theological Union. He has taught at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010), among other institutions.

Taijo Iwata worked in Buddhist studies. He held teaching posts at Rissho University (attested 1984) and Otani University (attested 1996), and served as an advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Taijun Inokuchi worked in Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1987) and served as representative of the Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. He served as professor of Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo from 1912.

Taiken Kyuma is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999 and served as an associate professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka studied at Hiroshima University and worked in Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Ryukoku University in 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Koyasan University and Toyo University (Ph.D., 1994). He has served on the faculty at Koyasan University, where he became a professor (attested 2005, 2026).
Taion Satomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1930–1933). He later served as a professor at Minobusan University (attested 1972).

Taira Shidehara was an archaeology and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1902) and Tokyo University of Education (~1900–1906).
